findings.summary: Two different external-linkage definitions of the same global C++ class Result are compiled into this checkpoint: the first defines value plus its constructor, while the second additionally defines failed() const. Neither type is TU-local or namespaced. Identical current size and exact machine-code matches do not satisfy the C++ one-definition rule: complete class definitions across translation units must agree. This is a concrete disagreement missed by the waived C++ mechanical audit, so both affected functions fail manual source/interface review. Repair: use one shared canonical Result declaration (including failed()) in both units, or evidence-backed distinct properly scoped types, then prepare a successor checkpoint and re-match both; do not mutate this sealed checkpoint.
